author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (concept and Meshy generation), brought inside its budget in-repo by the project's headless Blender pipeline
tool: Meshy (image-to-3D), run by the maintainer OUTSIDE this repository, then reduced inside it by tools/decimate_model.py (headless Blender 4.0.2): the Draco-compressed export was decoded, coincident vertices welded, 1,995,258 triangles collapse-decimated to 20,000, the 2048 maps kept at their source resolution, and the result gated on two-way surface deviation and on open edges. Uploaded as reference/coral_cove/Coral_Cove_Canopy_Tree_1.glb.
prompt: Generated by the maintainer in Meshy; the exact Meshy prompt is theirs and is not recorded in this repository. The dense source is kept in reference/coral_cove/ so the reduction can be re-run at any ratio. A GROVE, not a tree: six stylised broadleaf trees at assorted sizes on their own rock bases -- one large specimen with a broad flat crown and a second lower lobe, and five smaller ones scattered around it. Saturated teal-to-lime foliage over warm tan trunks, which sits squarely in the aquatic palette the art direction asks for. THE SIX TREES ARE ONE MESH. It can only be placed whole, so it is NOT a substitute for assets/environment/canopy_tree, the single generated tree that Coral Cove's ScatterFields scatter and that four named Dressing nodes place individually -- scattering this would plant six trees at every scatter point. Splitting the loose parts into separate assets is tracked work; until then this is a hand-placed set piece. Shipped at 20,000 triangles rather than the environment category's 200,000 ceiling, because what has to fit is the scene rather than the file; at that count the surface strays 0.42% of the bounding-box diagonal, well inside even the character-grade allowance, and a render at the shipped count shows the crowns, the sand caps and the coral dressing all intact.
licenseTerms: Meshy's terms of service govern the generated mesh and its maps; the maintainer generated the asset under their own Meshy account and contributed it to this repository. The in-repo Blender pass that reduces it is Apache-2.0 with the rest of the project, but it does not change the terms on the geometry it transforms. REVIEW NEEDED (REQ-021) before any redistribution that assumes a uniform Apache-2.0 grant over assets/: the project's promise to contributors is 'build your level out of our assets', which is a grant that cannot be made over geometry whose terms are someone else's.
